drhp.business: Manipal operates a pan-India network of multispecialty hospitals delivering care from outpatient services to complex tertiary and quaternary interventions. As of September 30, 2025 it ran 38 hospitals (48 on a pro forma basis) with 10,761 licensed beds (12,367 pro forma) across 14 states and union territories. Clinical focus is on tertiary/quaternary care in cardiac sciences, oncology, neurosciences, gastro sciences, orthopedics and renal sciences (CONGO-R).

drhp.expansion: Manipal plans to add approximately 751 licensed beds across existing hospitals and approximately 1,943 licensed beds through greenfield projects by 2030 to support growth. Its network grew from 28 hospitals with 7,699 licensed beds (Mar 31, 2023) to 48 hospitals with 12,367 licensed beds (pro forma, Sep 30, 2025), aided by acquisitions of AMRI (Sep 2023), Medica Synergie (Jul 2024) and Sahyadri (Oct 2025, adding 1,606 beds). In November 2025 it commenced its 49th hospital in Bengaluru, taking licensed capacity to 12,631 beds as of December 31, 2025.

Diversified clinical mix anchored in high-acuity tertiary/quaternary specialties (CONGO-R = 60-64% of gross inpatient revenue) supported by a captive DNB/DrNB/FNB training pipeline (343 seats, 659 students) and MAHE linkage.
Marquee institutional shareholder base (Temasek entities, TPG, Novo Holdings) and experienced management; strong brand recognition and NABH accreditation across 41 of 48 hospitals.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Karnataka hospitals contributed 51.55% of FY2025 revenue (66.61% in FY2023); disruption or policy change there would materially hurt results
- Growth relies heavily on acquisitions (AMRI, Medica Synergie, Sahyadri); failure to integrate/upgrade could erode expected synergies
- Pro forma information reflecting the Acquisition Transactions may not be indicative of actual or future results
- Six O&M hospitals operated under trust agreements (HCMCT, EIHF, KMMMT) carry contractual continuation risk
- ~49% of revenue from insurance/TPA and ~13% from government schemes exposes pricing to third-party and regulatory pressure
- Planned ~751 brownfield and ~1,943 greenfield beds by 2030 depend on capex, approvals and ramp-up timelines
- Business depends on licensed-bed approvals and NABH/NABL accreditations that can be withdrawn or delayed

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)

- **Acquire minority stake in stepdown Subsidiary Sahyadri Hospitals Private Limited from Fresh Issue Net Proceeds.**
- **Raise gross proceeds of the Fresh Issue of Rs 80,000 million (with a possible Pre-IPO Placement of up to Rs 16,000 million).**
- **Continue growing the high-acuity CONGO-R specialty mix (cardiac, oncology, neuro, gastro, ortho, renal) while maintaining operational efficiency.**
- **Integrate and upgrade acquired networks (AMRI, Medica Synergie, Sahyadri) within the Manipal network.**
